beats.text: The Voynich manuscript, a mysterious book from the 15th century.
Discovered in 1912 by Wilfrid Voynich, a Polish book dealer.
Carbon dating places it between 1404 and 1438, near modern-day Southern Germany, Switzerland, and Northern Italy.
beats.say: carbon dating 1404 1438 southern germany switzerland northern italy

beats.text: Its text, written in an undeciphered script called Voynichese, is undeciphered to this day.
The manuscript contains around 240 pages, mostly illustrated with strange diagrams and figures.
Experts believe it could be a hoax, a cipher, or a work of fiction.
Codebreakers from World War I and II, including Currier, Friedman, and Tiltman, failed to decipher it.
beats.say: codebreakers world war i ii currier friedman tiltman failed

beats.text: Yale University holds the manuscript in its Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library.
Follow ORDELVA for more on the Voynich manuscript.

facts.claim: Carbon dating places it between 1404 and 1438.
facts.quote: The results were consistent for all samples tested and indicated a date for the parchment between 1404 and 1438.
The manuscript consists of around 240 pages, but there is evidence that some of the pages are missing.

facts.claim: Codebreakers from World War I and II, including Currier, Friedman, and Tiltman, failed to decipher it.
facts.quote: Codebreakers Prescott Currier, William Friedman, Elizebeth Friedman, and John Tiltman were unsuccessful. The manuscript has never been demonstrably deciphered.
